report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Run all tasks, land every answer, return run summary; enforce spend guard and vote-temperature consistency.

symbols.name: fan_out
symbols.note: Main entry point: runs tasks via ThreadPoolExecutor, writes result files, installs budget guard.

claims.text: Never raises for a failing task: a fan-out of 1,200 in which one task dies must produce 1,199 answers and a named failure, not an exception.
claims.why: Exceptions from _run_task are caught in the as_completed loop (line ~359) and converted to a FanoutResult with errors; the loop continues.

claims.text: Transport failures are recorded on the result and the queue continues.
claims.why: _run_task catches per-vote exceptions (line ~343) and appends to res.errors; the thread pool continues with other tasks.

claims.text: resume skips any task whose result file already exists AND parses.
claims.why: Lines ~316-325 check dest.is_file(), parse JSON, and return a resumed result with prior data if parsed successfully.

claims.text: A file that exists but does not parse is re-run, because a truncated result is worse than a missing one.
claims.why: Lines ~326-328 catch (OSError, ValueError) and fall through to re-run; the file is overwritten later.

claims.text: asking for votes you cannot get is an error at the door
claims.why: Lines ~307-311 return a refused dict when any task has votes>1 and temperature<=0.0.

claims.text: At temperature 0.0 the decode is deterministic, so every vote returns the SAME answer
claims.why: This claims a property of the model decode that is not observable in this chunk; it depends on the provider behavior.

claims.text: Fail CLOSED: a fan-out whose spend cannot be capped does not run.
claims.why: Lines ~332-341 return a refused dict if install_process_guard raises.

claims.text: SAME SUMMARY SHAPE as a completed run, including paid_calls and results.
claims.why: The refusal dict at lines ~336-340 includes all keys: state, reason, tasks, ok, failed, resumed, paid_calls, out_dir, concurrency, results.

claims.text: NOT re-stamped: the prior trace is the run that paid for this answer.
claims.why: Line ~323 sets trace_id=prior.get("trace_id") instead of the current trace variable.

claims.text: PAID CALLS, separate from task count: with votes>1 they differ
claims.why: counts["calls"] is incremented per vote in _run_task (line ~347) and returned as paid_calls; task count is len(tasks).

claims.text: a ledger total is a ceiling and never an invoice
claims.why: This claim about the budget ledger's pricing semantics is not verifiable from this chunk; it references behavior in another module.

claims.text: A refusal that returns a different dict forces every consumer to write two code paths
claims.why: The refusal dicts (both guard failure and vote temperature) match the success dict's key set, except state differs.

observations.what: The guard installation is attempted with a try/except that catches all exceptions and refuses to run, but the comment says 'Fail CLOSED' yet the code returns a refused dict rather than raising; this is consistent with the stated policy.
on_result callback exceptions are silently swallowed with a pass comment, which could hide a broken callback; the docstring says 'must not kill the queue' but does not mention the swallowing.
The vote-temperature refusal returns a dict with 'state': 'refused' but the summary docstring only mentions 'ran' state; consumers may not expect this state value.

The result file is written atomically (write_text_atomic) but the comment about 'resume' says a file that exists but does not parse is re-run; the code catches OSError and ValueError only, not a general JSONDecodeError (which is a subclass of ValueError, so covered).

The 'resumed' count is incremented only when res.answers is truthy; if a prior file exists and parses but has empty answers, it is re-run and not counted as resumed, which is consistent with the docstring.

risks: lines ~366-369 | medium | on_result callback exceptions are silently swallowed, hiding potential consumer bugs; a failing callback is invisible and the queue continues, which may be intended but is undocumented | Check if the docstring or tests specify callback error handling
